subject: community-medicine
title: Poliomyelitis and viral hepatitis: high-yield essentials for NEET-PG and INI-CET

steps.tx: **Poliomyelitis** is caused by polioviruses, enteroviruses of three types. Most infections are asymptomatic, and fewer than one in a hundred infections cause paralysis. Death in paralytic polio is usually due to **respiratory insufficiency**. Faeco-oral spread through contaminated food, water or hands is the usual route. Virus can be shed in stool for several weeks, so the stool must be tested early.

steps.tx: **Acute flaccid paralysis** surveillance detects every child under 15 with sudden limb weakness, because polio is only one cause. Guillain-Barre syndrome and transverse myelitis also present this way. A case is confirmed as polio when wild poliovirus is isolated from stool. Residual weakness at 60 days supports a **polio compatible** classification when stool is inadequate.

steps.tx: Two vaccines exist. **IPV**, the inactivated vaccine, is safe in immunodeficiency and pregnancy, gives no herd immunity, and needs four doses. **OPV**, the live attenuated trivalent vaccine, induces both local and systemic immunity, drives herd immunity and is used in epidemics. OPV is contraindicated in AIDS and immunocompromised persons, and it can cause vaccine associated paralysis.

steps.tx: **Pulse polio immunisation** was first run by the Government of India in December 1995 and January 1996. It gives one extra OPV dose to all children under 5, regardless of past immunisation, on a single day. Rounds fall in the low transmission season, November to February, because peak transmission in India is June to September. The **reverse cold chain** returns stool samples from AFP cases to the laboratory.

steps.tx: Three vaccine derived types matter. **cVDPV** shows person to person spread in the community. **iVDPV** comes from people with primary immunodeficiency who shed virus for prolonged periods. **aVDPV** is ambiguous, from a person without known immunodeficiency or from sewage. Eradication is certified regionally after at least three consecutive years without wild poliovirus transmission.

steps.tx: In **hepatitis B**, **HBsAg** is the first marker in serum and the epidemiological marker for endemicity. HBeAg marks active replication and high infectivity. Anti-HBs alone indicates recovery or vaccine protection. IgM anti-HBc signals acute infection. Newborns of HBeAg positive mothers face over 90 percent transmission, so HBIG plus vaccine within 12 hours of birth is given.
